title: Antigravity CLI settings
description: Settings for Antigravity CLI, stored in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. Every key is optional, and a key you leave out uses its default. The CLI keeps keys it doesn't recognize. Documentation: https://antigravity.google/docs/settings?tab=cli

$schema.description: URL of this schema, for editor autocomplete and validation. The CLI ignores it.

agentMode.description: Execution mode the CLI starts in: "" (default mode, which asks before file edits), "accept-edits" (approves workspace file edits automatically), "auto" (approves edits and safe commands, and asks before irreversible actions; CLI 1.3.5+ on macOS and Linux and 1.4.4+ on Windows, needs the terminal sandbox, and isn't available for business or enterprise accounts), or "plan" (researches and plans before making changes). --mode overrides it for one session. If agentMode isn't set, CLI 1.5.7+ starts in "auto" where it's available and in default mode otherwise; set "" to always start in default mode. If "auto" isn't available, the CLI starts in default mode.

allowNonWorkspaceAccess.description: Lets the agent read and edit files outside your workspace folders, subject to toolPermission, agentMode, and your permission rules. /config: Non-Workspace Access.

altScreenMode.description: How the TUI uses the terminal: "default" renders the conversation inline and opens full-screen views in the alternate screen, "always" runs the whole TUI in the alternate screen, and "never" never uses the alternate screen. /config: Rendering Mode ("never" is available only here).

artifactReviewPolicy.description: Whether the agent waits for your review when it asks for feedback on an artifact, such as an implementation plan: "asks-for-review" always waits, "agent-decides" currently works the same as "asks-for-review", and "always-proceed" never waits. It doesn't affect file edits. /config: Artifact Review.

clearScrollbackOnResize.description: In inline rendering, clears the terminal scrollback when the CLI redraws the conversation, such as after you resize the window.

colorScheme.description: Color theme. "terminal" uses your terminal's colors. /config: Color Scheme.

copyOnSelect.description: In alt-screen mode, copies text to the clipboard when you release a mouse selection. When false, the artifact viewer uses your terminal's own text selection. /config: Copy on Select.

customModelsConfig.description: Extra models for /model when you use a Gemini API key. The CLI reads it only when modelProvider is "gemini" and GEMINI_API_KEY is set, and ignores it when you sign in with a Google Account.

disableSlashCommands.description: In headless mode (-p), sends prompts that start with / to the model as typed instead of running slash commands or skills. Same as --disable-slash-commands.

editor.description: External editor for opening artifacts and files and for composing prompts (Ctrl+G). "auto" uses $EDITOR, then falls back to vim (macOS and Linux) or to edit and notepad (Windows). Any other value is run as the editor command. /config: Editor.

editorMode.description: Editing model for the prompt: "default" or "vim" (modal editing). /config: Editor Mode.

enableTelemetry.description: Not read from settings.json. Enable Telemetry in /config is saved with your account, and the CLI removes this key when it saves the file.

enableTerminalSandbox.description: Runs the agent's terminal commands in the terminal sandbox. Since CLI 1.4.4, it has no effect where the sandbox isn't available. --sandbox turns it on for one session. /config: Sandbox Mode.

gcp.description: Saved by the "Use a Google Cloud project" sign-in option, which uses it to fill in the next sign-in. You don't need to edit it.

hideActiveItems.description: Hides the list of active subagents and background tasks below the prompt box. /config: Show Active Tasks (inverted).

historySize.description: Number of prompt history entries kept on disk. The CLI trims the history when it exits: -1 keeps every entry, and 0 clears the history.

hooks.description: Not read from settings.json. Put hooks in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json or <workspace>/.agents/hooks.json instead.

model.description: The model chosen with /model, saved by its label. If it's no longer available, the CLI uses the default model and shows a warning.

modelProvider.description: Set to "gemini" to send model requests directly to the Gemini API with the key in GEMINI_API_KEY.

notifications.description: Rings the terminal bell and shows a desktop notification when the agent needs your approval or an answer, or finishes its turn. /config: Notifications.

permissions.description: Allow, ask, and deny rules for the agent's tools (the Global scope in /permissions). A deny rule takes precedence over an ask rule, and an ask rule over an allow rule.

pickerGrouping.description: How the /resume picker lists conversations: "none" (one list, most recent first) or "grouped" (grouped by workspace). /config: Conversation Picker Grouping.

queuedMessages.description: What happens to a message you send while the agent is working: "queue" holds it until the current turn ends, and "send-immediately" interrupts the agent and sends it right away. /config: Queued Messages.

runningLightSpeed.description: Speed of the progress indicator animation. /config: Animation Speed.

sandboxProxy.description: Sends network traffic from sandboxed terminal commands through your own HTTP proxy instead of the built-in one. It applies only while the terminal sandbox is on, and your proxy then has to enforce any read_url rules.

showFeedbackSurvey.description: Shows a brief feedback survey from time to time after a task finishes. /config: Show Feedback Survey.

showTips.description: Shows usage tips while the agent is generating a response. /config: Show Tips.

anyOf.description: Not recommended: a boolean is read as an object without a command, so no script runs.

statusLine.description: Runs your own script to draw the status line below the prompt box.

anyOf.description: Not recommended: a boolean is read as an object without a command, so no script runs.

title.description: Runs your own script to set the terminal window title.

toolPermission.description: When the agent asks before using a tool: "request-review" asks before write, bash, web, and MCP tools unless an allow rule covers them; "proceed-in-sandbox" runs terminal commands without asking when the sandbox is on and the command runs inside it (since CLI 1.4.4, it works like "request-review" where the sandbox isn't available); "always-proceed" runs commands, web requests, and MCP tools without asking unless an ask or deny rule matches; and "strict" asks before every tool action, including file reads, even if an allow rule matches. Deny rules apply in every mode. /config: Tool Permission.

trustedWorkspaces.description: Folders you chose to trust when the CLI asked. The CLI adds entries for you.

useG1Credits.description: Uses your AI credits for model requests after your plan's quota runs out. Not available for business accounts. /config: Use AI Credits.

useTerminalCursor.description: Uses your terminal's own cursor shape instead of a block cursor.

verbosity.description: How much of the agent's work the conversation shows: "high" shows every tool call, command, and thought in full; "medium" groups related tool calls and thoughts into summaries while keeping commands and responses visible; and "low" shows only responses and collapses tool activity into a token usage summary. /config: Verbosity.

vimInsertFirst.description: When editorMode is "vim", starts the prompt in Insert mode and makes a bare Enter submit. /config: Editor Mode › Insert First.

permissionRule.description: A rule in the form action(target), with no space before the parenthesis. Actions: command, read_file, write_file, read_url, execute_url, and mcp (unsandboxed for business and enterprise accounts). For example: command(git status), read_file(/var/log), read_url(github.com), or mcp(github/*). The CLI ignores rules it can't parse.

allow.description: Actions the agent may take without asking.

ask.description: Actions the agent always asks about first.

deny.description: Actions the agent may never take. Deny rules take precedence over ask and allow rules.

type.description: Optional. "command" is the only supported type.

command.description: Shell command to run, through sh -c (cmd /c on Windows). It receives the session state as JSON on stdin, and its output becomes the status line. Multi-line output and ANSI colors are supported, and a leading ~ expands to your home directory.

padding.description: Number of blank lines above the status line.

enabled.description: Set to false to stop running command and show the built-in status line instead. The command stays in settings.json.

stack_with_default.description: When true, shows your status line below the built-in one instead of replacing it.

type.description: Optional. "command" is the only supported type.

command.description: Shell command to run, through sh -c (cmd /c on Windows). It receives the session state as JSON on stdin, and its output becomes the window title: lines are joined with spaces and control characters are removed, so print one line of plain text.

enabled.description: Set to false to stop updating the title. The command stays in settings.json.

customModels.description: Custom models by key. The key or the label selects the model in /model or --model.

modelName.description: Required. The model to call, in the form gemini-api://<base_url>/models/<model>.

label.description: Name shown in /model. Defaults to "Custom Model: <model>".

maxTokens.description: Context window size in tokens, including the response.

modelFeatures.description: Capabilities of the model. Each one is true unless you set it to false.

toolFormatterType.description: How tools are presented to the model. TOOL_FORMATTER_TYPE_NONE uses the model API's native tool calling. Unrecognized values fall back to TOOL_FORMATTER_TYPE_XML.

apiProvider.description: Optional. Leave it unset; the CLI infers the provider from modelName.

http.description: HTTP proxy settings. address and certFile go together, and so do username and password; if either pair is incomplete, the CLI ignores sandboxProxy.

certFile.description: Path to the proxy's CA certificate, which the sandbox trusts.
